stories.title: School meal review includes portion size and cold options
stories.summary: The Cabinet is to discuss proposals to overhaul the free hot school meals programme after two Government-commissioned reviews revealed shortcomings in the service. Minister for Social Protection Dara Calleary will outline to the Cabinet the findings of two independent studies examining food standards and student, parent and teacher experience on the School Meals Programme. Mr Calleary will seek Cabinet approval for a number of changes to the scheme, after it was discovered that roughly a fifth of all hot school meals - or around 100,000 a day - go uneaten. When accounting for absences, the proportion of uneaten meals is 11.1%. Around half a million hot school meals are delivered to primary schools across the country daily, with the scheme extended nationwide in September 2025 to benefit 3,200 schools and more than 550,000 children. However, the €300 million scheme has faced some criticism, with the Oireachtas Committee on Education hearing concerns earlier this year around the nutritional quality of meals, including the level of highly processed foods and the lack of transparency regarding production methods.

stories.title: One person still in hospital after prison overdoses
stories.summary: The Irish Prison Service said that one person from the Midlands Prison remains in hospital following a series of overdoses on Friday. It said the issue was localised within the Midlands Prison and following a targeted security operation and information campaign, no further overdoses have presented since. In a statement it said: "We continue to work with the HSE to identify the drug concerned and are engaged with An Garda Síochána to identify the source of the drug." It described the assault on two staff on Friday as "unacceptable" and said the matter has been referred to gardaí for investigation. Four prisoners were hospitalised yesterday as a result of overdoses, after drugs were dropped by drone into a prison yard, according to a source. Social Democrats TD Gary Gannon described what happened in Midlands Prison as "worrying" and that he believes it reflects "that there has been an increasing normalisation of addiction in prison".

stories.title: McEntee declines to back calls for disclosures inquiry
stories.summary: Garda representative bodies and opposition politicians have called for an inquiry with the Association of Garda Sergeants and Inspectors, saying that they have "serious concerns around the independence of the protected disclosures process" within the garda force. The former Minister for Justice also insisted she will not consider her position at Cabinet in light of the revelations contained within the broadcast. Speaking at a Fine Gael conference for small businesses in Dublin today, Ms McEntee reiterated on a number of occasions her position from the Dáil on Thursday that she had "adhered to the law at all times" when it came to protected disclosures during her time at the Department of Justice. "That's a matter for the Minister for Justice, that's not for me to decide," said the Meath East TD when asked should there be a public inquiry into the issues. "My understanding is he's [Jim O'Callaghan] made a decision on that this morning [not to hold an inquiry] so I'm not going to cross over that," she added. On calls for urgent action to ensure the protected disclosure process within An Garda Síochána is independent, Ms McEntee again refrained from offering a viewpoint, saying it was a matter for the Minister for Justice.

stories.title: Oil at 1 week low on hopes of boost to diplomacy in war
stories.summary: Oil prices slid to their lowest in more than a week today on hopes diplomacy in the Iran war will get a chance this week amid a UN meet and as investors eyed a partial recovery in shipments from Saudi Arabia despite ongoing attacks by Yemen's Houthis. Brent crude futures and US West Texas Intermediate crude touched their lowest since September 10 earlier today, with Brent at $101.71 a barrel, down $2.16, or 2.08%, after settling 0.91% lower on Friday. US West Texas Intermediate crude lost $2.15, or 2.14%, to $98.15 a barrel following a 1.58% drop in the previous session. "It seems that a degree of risk premium is being removed from oil prices on hopes that a diplomatic path to de-escalate the US-Iran war may arrive this week," Tim Waterer, chief market analyst at KCM Trade, said. "Whether that hope proves to be warranted or not is another question. Time will tell." The WTI broke a key psychological support at $100 a barrel while some investors may have rolled over their positions in the October contract a day ahead of expiry to November, a Singapore-based broker said.

stories.title: US-Greenland deal reaffirms 'Danish sovereignty' - Macron
stories.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron said a deal between the United States, Denmark and Greenland helps "to reaffirm Danish sovereignty" over the Arctic territory. "I simply note that Danish sovereignty is respected, that international law is respected, and that this is what we were asking for. So it's a good thing," Mr Macron said while visiting the French overseas territory of Saint Pierre and Miquelon. Earlier, Denmark hailed the "binding" deal announced by US President Donald Trump to give Washington "permanent control" over Greenland's security and bar Russian and Chinese bases from the Arctic territory. Since returning to the White House in January 2025, Mr Trump has repeatedly insisted that the United States needed to control Greenland for strategic reasons, alarming NATO ally Denmark and sparking fierce pushback from the alliance. Denmark and Greenland - an autonomous Danish territory - both hailed the agreement and said they would sign it on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York next week. "A long period of uncertainty will hopefully be replaced by a binding agreement that strengthens security in the Arctic and North Atlantic," Danish Foreign Minister Lars Lokke Rasmussen said on social media.

stories.title: USA defeat doesn't dampen debut feeling for Adams Verling
stories.summary: A 40-36 defeat to the USA means it won't go down as a dream debut for Ireland’s latest international Jemima Adams Verling, but the Connacht back row insists her first cap is still "the most incredible experience" of her life. The 20-year-old played 50 minutes on debut at Tallaght Stadium yesterday and looked at home in Test rugby, logging a whopping 16 tackles in just 50 minutes on the pitch. Ireland were 31-12 in front and seemingly cruising against Jack Hanratty’s side when Adams Verling was replaced by Brittany Hogan with 30 minutes to play. But even the second half collapse did little to quench her enthusiasm as she reflected on her first cap. "It's always unfortunate to come out with a loss at the back of the game but it was just the most incredible experience of my life and I've just so much pride for the girls," Adams Verling said. "They put their hearts out there and the intent I saw from all of them, even when I came off, they were absolutely impeccable.

stories.title: Leitrim's Casey ready for more after faithfulness tested
stories.summary: No word of a lie, Donal Casey's life has changed utterly in the past 12 months. A year ago this weekend, the then 23-year-old was in game mode, an interested spectator in the crowd as the Leitrim SFC quarter-finals were playing out. Nothing really mattered at that time apart from a manic determination to help Leitrim Gaels, who had safely navigated a path to the semi-finals, get their hands on the Fenagh Perpetual Cup for the first time in the club’s history. Life's most valuable information in that moment was finding out who would be facing Mal Guckian’s side in the last four. He did help his club to that coveted silverware, but life isn’t just about football anymore. After what happened in that county final, his outlook changed forever. Back to that 2025 county final though and the victory over Sean O’Heslin’s. It was a day when dreams should have been realised, but for the young centre half-back, it came so close to complete tragedy.

stories.title: Celtic slump continues in derby defeat to Rangers
stories.summary: Rangers racked up a second win over Celtic in eight days as boos rung around an all-green Parkhead following a 1-0 defeat by the Light Blues. Celtic's 74-year-old boss Martin O’Neill went into the game under the spotlight after two successive losses, including a bruising 3-0 Premier Sports Cup clash with the Gers at Ibrox last Sunday. To silence inside a stadium populated with home fans only, Gers striker Ryan Naderi opened the scoring in the 33rd minute and it was enough for another huge victory for Derek McInnes’s men who will feel they should have added to that goal after the break. It was a first William Hill Premiership defeat of the season for the home side, who are just two points ahead of their Glasgow rivals at the top of the table going into the international break with more pressure on O’Neill. Due to a ticket allocation spat between the two city rivals which saw the authorities step in, there were only Gers fans inside Ibrox last week and only Hoops supporters at Celtic Park and they suffered another torturous 90 minutes. In a frenetic start, Gers winger Djeidi Gassama got in behind the defence but failed to finish.

stories.title: Preview: Ireland out to keep ball rolling against USA
stories.summary: When this Ireland team made their big breakthrough at WXV1 in Canada this time two years ago, it was their phenomenal and shock win against the world champions New Zealand that made headlines. A little less notable, but just as important, was their 26-14 win against the USA in Vancouver two weeks later, which proved the Black Ferns win was no fluke, and that Scott Bemand's side were a group to watch. At the time, it was an Ireland squad still finding their feet and light on experience; current captain Erin King was in the first few games of her XVs career, Aoife Wafer was a raw talent, while Dannah O’Brien had yet to fully make the number 10 jersey her own. Of the 15 players that started against the USA two years ago, 11 will play a part this afternoon, while Clíodhna Moloney-MacDonald, Eve Higgins and O’Brien all played from the bench. In terms of personnel, there hasn’t been a great deal of change to the Ireland squad in the last couple of seasons, a sign of the age-profile in the group. However, the level of expectation around this side has changed dramatically. In the two years since that game, Ireland have cemented their place as the best of the rest in women’s rugby.

stories.title: U2 at 50: The 10 best U2 songs of all time, ranked
stories.summary: Freelance journalist and broadcaster, writing about music and the arts. Happy Birthday, U2! One of the biggest rock bands of all time celebrates 50 years in business this month, with 15 studio albums, 12 EPs, three compilations, two live albums and no less than 85 singles released by the Dublin band over the course of that half-century. The question is, which songs are their best? It may be overplayed, it may be somewhat overcooked, it may not have the emotional heft of some of their other tracks - but only a curmudgeon would argue against Beautiful Day being one of U2’s most euphoric songs. Taken from 2001’s pivotal All That You Can’t Leave Behind album, it ushered in a new era for the band while cementing their position as one of the finest stadium rock bands on the planet. That intro alone is worth its weight in gold: the yearning squeal of The Edge’s guitar, the piano riff, the tremulous bassline, that primitive yowl of Bono’s…. 43 years after it was first released, New Year’s Day sounds as fresh as ever. The first track from U2’s third album War also incorporated social and political themes, written about the revolutionary Polish solidarity movement in 1980 which eventually led to the collapse of communism in Poland. Apparently it was originally intended as a love song about Ali Hewson. No harm, no foul, Ali. U2 have always looked to the wider world for inspiration, but this song - also taken from War - brought them closer to home and is perhaps their most explicitly political song to date. Written about the Troubles and specifically the Bloody Sunday atrocity of 1972, it’s a protest song about the futility of war, wrapped up in a spiky rock tune. From Larry Mullen’s martial cadence to Bono’s exasperated lyrics ("How long, how long must we sing this song?"), it still packs a mighty punch. By 1987, U2 had spent much of the decade touring extensively in America and absorbing its culture from the inside looking out. The result was The Joshua Tree - the album that many fans still consider their defining moment. stories.title: Richard Hammond marks jet car crash anniversary
stories.summary: Former Top Gear presenter Richard Hammond has thanked emergency workers on the 20th anniversary of his jet car crash. The 56-year-old suffered serious injuries in the 320mph crash in 2006, while driving the jet-powered Vampire dragster during filming for the BBC motoring show at the former RAF Elvington airbase near York. In a post on Instagram, Hammond said: "20 years ago today, I came to an abrupt stop upside down in a Yorkshire field, convinced I was about to die. "A front tyre had blown on the jet-powered dragster I had been driving at over 300mph. "I had pulled the lever to release the parachute and done my best to steer the car away from disaster, but disaster was, it seemed, my fate and having done everything I could do avert it, I gave myself over to that fate." Hammond went on to say that he "didn't scream" during the incident and said it "wasn’t frightening", adding that "it simply occurred to me that the next thing on my to do list was to die".

stories.title: Irish designer Simone Rocha bares all at London Fashion Week
stories.summary: One of Britain’s most famous criminal courts became an unlikely setting for exposed underwear and bare skin as Irish designer Simone Rocha brought her London Fashion Week show to the Old Bailey. The Dublin-born designer, known for her heavily layered dresses, frills and floral embellishments, took a noticeably less covered-up approach to her spring/summer 2027 collection, sending models through the marble halls of London’s Central Criminal Court in sheer dresses, open leather jackets and little more than underwear. It was a departure for Rocha, whose clothes often conceal the body beneath layers of tulle, tailoring and exaggerated skirts. Speaking backstage, she said she deliberately wanted this collection to feel more vulnerable. "Sometimes I can be very layered, and I can really put clothes on top of clothes; it’s a very protective thing, and I wanted to be this slightly more vulnerable," she said. One model wore a black leather jacket with a plunging neckline that extended almost to the waist, its lapels decorated with oversized leather roses.

stories.title: Political attention set as Budget 2027 on the horizon
stories.summary: Aside from the ongoing fallout from the latest garda whistleblower revelations; political attention is now set to hone in on the Budget to be announced on Tuesday fortnight. The Coalition enters this season's edition in somewhat of a bind. Pressure is mounting that Budget 2027 not be an underwhelming one for the general public, but ongoing global uncertainty means it is impossible to know just how much must be set aside and for how long fuel supports must continue. Bilateral talks began last week in Government Buildings with Cabinet figures presenting their wish lists to Minister for Public Expenditure Jack Chambers and Minister for Finance Simon Harris. The Coalition has vowed to keep spending growth at 6% or lower in 2027 but according to those involved in the talks, that didn't stop some Government ministers presenting with lengthy scrolls of budgetary asks. One insider described the talks as a "mixed bag" with some departments coming forward with "very ambitious asks well above the 6% growth rate already agreed".

stories.title: Housing and the cost of living highlighted during protest
stories.summary: A number of trade unions and political activists marched in Dublin, calling for action on housing and the cost of living ahead of Budget 2027. SIPTU, Unite, Fórsa, and others gathered at the Garden of Remembrance to walk to Leinster House where a rally took place. Political parties such as People Before Profit, Solidarity, Sinn Féin and the Social Democrats were among those present. "The central contradiction in Ireland today is that we have a wealthy economy but the workers who create that wealth are being priced out of a decent life," SIPTU Sector Organiser Paddy Cole said before the protest. He added: "Whether people rent or hope to buy, too much of their wages is swallowed by housing. Workers from home and abroad can have qualifications, full-time jobs and good wages, yet still be unable to leave the family home, rent a decent place to live or plan for children. "That is an abject policy failure, not a failure of the people who are trying to do all the right things. This crisis unites healthcare assistants, retail workers, civil servants, hospitality workers, construction workers, transport workers and many others. Governments respond when people organise and put them under pressure."

stories.title: German car workers hold protests after VW profit warning
stories.summary: German car workers staged nationwide protests today, less than three days after a shock profit warning by Europe's biggest auto maker Volkswagen highlighted the sector's unprecedented challenges from high costs and fierce Asian rivals. The protests at Volkswagen, BMW and parts supplier Bosch come as Germany's most important industry faces painful job cuts, possible production relocations and even plant closures, a crisis that was also reflected in the result of two state elections over the weekend. "Due to lethargy and disastrous misjudgements, most managers have failed to keep pace with developments in e-mobility, digitalisation and battery technology, thereby causing the German automotive and supplier industries to fall behind," Horst Ott of trade union IG Metall said. European automakers are facing increased competition from Asian rivals abroad and at home, creating a major problem for Volkswagen, which is already battling overcapacity on the continent, US tariffs and plunging profits in China. Volkswagen on Friday cut its profit margin outlook for 2026 to 1% at the most, blaming the sluggish Chinese market and higher provisions for retirements but also sobering expectations for its Porsche sportscar brand. Part of the problem was accelerated demand for less profitable electric vehicles, underscoring the sector's ongoing dependence on combustion engines that have for decades fuelled Germany's top economy.

stories.title: Ireland to navigate relationships at UN General Assembly
stories.summary: World leaders will gather in New York this week for the 81st United Nations General Assembly, at a time of war, mounting global instability and growing pressure on the organisation itself. The UN has warned of a world facing more than 120 conflicts, as it grapples with its own serious funding crisis. Earlier this year, UN Secretary-General António Guterres warned that the organisation was facing "imminent financial collapse". The Taoiseach and senior Government ministers, including Foreign Affairs Minister Helen McEntee, will travel to New York this week for a series of events. Micheál Martin will be one of nearly 130 heads of state and government attending High-Level Week. Throughout the week, leaders are scheduled to take to the podium to deliver their national statements, which usually set out a country's international priorities.

stories.title: Former Ireland international McDonagh dies aged 64
stories.summary: Former Ireland international centre half Jack 'Jacko' McDonagh has passed away at the age of 64, his former club Shamrock Rovers announced on Monday. McDonagh represented Ireland at senior level three times for the Republic of Ireland under the managership of Eoin Hand across 1983 and 1984, having had a stellar career domestically and a brief stint in France and Belgium. Hailing from Donnybrook originally, McDonagh started his career with the Shelbourne youths before making the switch to Bohemians. During this spell, he won the PFAI Young Player of the Year for the 1981-82 season. He played 60 times across three seasons with the Gypsies before making the switch south to Rovers. McDonagh played on the four-in-a-row team in 1983/84 and 1984/85, the latter season having won the league and FAI Cup double. Also in 1983, he would make his Ireland debut under Hand, as they defeated Malta 8-0 in Dalymount Park.

stories.title: Dunne doubts there's appetite for more GAA rule changes
stories.summary: Former Offaly forward Nigel Dunne has questioned whether there is a sufficient appetite amongst the GAA public for further rule changes in Gaelic football. Several tweaks will be trialled over the coming months in third level Ryan Cup fixtures, following research and discussion amongst members of the Expert Advisory Group, which is chaired by former Mayo player and manager Kevin McStay. The EAG - which was formed following the work of the Football Review Committee - is charged with monitoring trends in the game and has come up with a number of proposals to be introduced in the coming months. Among the key proposals is the banning of fisted points (unless the ball is already in flight), limiting the number of consecutive handpasses to three and awarding four points for a goal. A backcourt rule, whereby the ball cannot return back over the halfway line, and a modified kickout rule, where the ball is no longer required to travel beyond the two-point arc, are also included in the slate of changes. "In isolation they're fine and I don’t disagree with them but the problem is why change now?

stories.title: Leeds extend unbeaten start in Crystal Palace stalemate
stories.summary: Leeds extended their unbeaten start to the season but had to settle for a point from a goalless draw with much-improved Crystal Palace at Elland Road. Dominic Calvert-Lewin spurned Leeds' best chance when firing straight at Palace goalkeeper Walter Benitez in the second half after visiting defender Tyrick Mitchell was denied a winner by VAR. These are heady times at Leeds after they climbed up to third in the table last week after dismantling Newcastle 4-1 and although they are only five games into their second season back in the top flight, expectation was high among fans before kick-off. But Palace turned in one of their best displays of the season and will consider themselves unlucky to have secured only one point after creating the better chances. Given Palace had conceded more goals – 11 – than any other side in the top flight this season, it was no surprise they sat deep when out of possession in the early exchanges. But they were dangerous on the counter-attack and it took a superb recovery tackle from Tarik Muharemovic to deny Jorgen Strand Larsen, while Leeds squandered early pressure with poor set-piece deliveries.

stories.summary: Star Wars production company Lucasfilm has sent congratulations to the team behind Spider-Man: Brand New Day after it became the highest-grossing film of all time in North America. Lucasfilm wrote on social media: "Impressive. Most impressive. "From a galaxy far, far away, everyone at Lucasfilm sends massive congratulations to Destin, Tom, everyone at Sony Pictures and Marvel Studios and the entire team behind Spider-Man: Brand New Day on setting a new domestic box office record and taking the crown from Star Wars: The Force Awakens." The company shared an animated photo of Spider-Man throwing his hands in the air along with a message reading: "The force is strong with you! Congratulations from Lucasfilm." The Spider-Man: Brand New Day Instagram account also posted a message acknowledging the record, writing: "Doesn't get bigger than this.

stories.title: Maura Derrane on bold fashion statements and working with Dáithí
stories.summary: As she returns to the Today show for a 15th season, Maura Derrane tells Clare O'Mahony why she thinks the show chimes with its viewers, how her innate curiosity makes it her natural media home and getting evil with Dáithí Ó Sé just before they go on air, "Everywhere I go in Ireland, and even away, if you meet an Irish person, they’re like, 'When are you back to the show?’," says Maura Derrane. "It’s become a staple, and I think that’s so brilliant." She says she had just such queries recently while shopping, as one person after another asked when Today would be returning after its summer break. 14 years on air, the programme is woven into the rhythm of its viewers’ lives, ending as the summer begins and returning as children settle back into school. "It’s a kind of home from home in Cork, and a lot of the people I work with have been there since the beginning. There’s a real family feeling because we’re not a big team, but we’ve been together for a long time." The summer break gave Maura time for trips to Italy and Portugal, although much of her summer was spent at home on Inis Mór. Her mother Bridgie is now 90, and those weeks allow Maura to make up for time away during the working year. She says that Cal, who has a cousin a few years older there, loves the island too. Going home also means returning to the garden and food she grew up with. Her family has always grown potatoes and vegetables in a centuries-old way, using seaweed gathered on the island’s shore, while her sister Barbara, who is also an artist, now grows grapes in a polytunnel. "She’s totally exotic down there," Maura laughs. "She’s like Tahiti-slash-Inis Mór!"

stories.title: Taoiseach and ministers head for UN General Assembly
stories.summary: The Taoiseach and several Government ministers are travelling to New York today for the 81st United Nations General Assembly High-Level Week. This annual gathering of presidents, prime ministers and other senior officials takes place against the backdrop of war and instability in the Middle East, the continuing war in Ukraine, and questions over the future role and operations of the United Nations itself. The Taoiseach will represent Ireland at UN High-Level Week, along with Minister for Foreign Affairs and Trade Helen McEntee, Minister for Climate, Environment and Energy Darragh O'Brien, Minister of State for International Development and Diaspora Neale Richmond, and Minister of State at the Department of Climate, Energy and the Environment, with special responsibility for the Marine, Timmy Dooley. The first day of the high-level general debate will be on tomorrow, under the main theme 'Restoring trust, managing transformation: a United Nations that delivers for all'. Analysis: Ireland must navigate diplomatic relationships at UN General Assembly The Government has greater diplomatic visibility this year, as Ireland holds the Presidency of the Council of the European Union.

stories.summary: The founder of a GAA club in Kyiv in Ukraine has described how the worsening situation with Russian attacks on the capital city is impacting on life there and on the recently formed club. The team competed in the Central East GAA Regional Finals which were held during this year's Tocatí festival in Verona of which Ireland was guest of honour. The first, for it to be a focal point for the Irish Community in Kyiv but also to create a space for the thousands of Ukrainians who are currently involved with clubs throughout Ireland. "There are thousands of Ukrainians involved in GAA with schools and clubs throughout Ireland. We wanted to create a space for them when the war is over and they return home, we will welcome them back and they will have a place to continue to play our games," he said.

stories.title: JD Sports expands into Mexico with Grupo Axo partnership
stories.summary: UK sportswear retailer JD Sports today announced its expansion into Mexico through a long-term franchise partnership with fashion retailer Grupo Axo, betting on strong demand from Mexico's growing young population. JD cut its profit outlook after weak demand from its core younger and less affluent customer base hit its North American market of US and Canada, which accounts for over a third of its sales. Under the agreement, Axo will operate JD stores and e-commerce in Mexico, using JD's brand and intellectual property, with the two companies also leveraging JD's own-brand and exclusive product portfolio across footwear, apparel and accessories. JD said Axo will operate more than 140 of its premises in the country, through Axo's existing sneaker stores, with plans to upsize stores at key locations over time. "We see a significant opportunity to lead the category in Mexico" said CEO Régis Schultz. The deal expands JD's franchise platform, which currently spans 75 JD and Courir franchise stores across Europe, the Middle East, Africa and Asia.

stories.title: US military says four killed in Caribbean boat strike
stories.summary: The US military announced that four people had been killed in a strike on a boat it said was involved in drug smuggling in the Caribbean. "Confirmed intelligence revealed the vessel's active involvement in narco-trafficking. The operation killed four narco-terrorists," SOUTHCOM, which commands US forces in the region, said in a statement, along with a grainy video of the attack on the boat. The US military launched operation "Southern Spear" in early September, with US President Donald Trump arguing Washington is effectively at war with drug cartels operating out of Latin America. Since then, more than 200 people have been killed in strikes in the Caribbean Sea and Eastern Pacific Ocean, according to a tally. Mr Trump's administration has not provided definitive evidence that the vessels it has been striking are involved in drug trafficking. Legal experts and rights groups say the strikes could amount to extrajudicial killings.

stories.title: Carrick: We can learn about ourselves in the tough times
stories.summary: Michael Carrick said fine margins are costing Manchester United after a 1-1 draw against Fulham stretched their winless Premier League run to three matches. United were fortunate to leave Craven Cottage with a point thanks to Matheus Cunha's 89th-minute deflected goal, though it was not enough to lift them out of the bottom half of the table heading into the international break. A muted display took a comedic turn when Lisandro Martinez stabbed the ball into his own net just past the hour mark, the defender seemingly caught by surprise after goalkeeper Senne Lammens had fumbled a Calvin Bassey shot with his legs. It neatly summarised the mess Carrick’s side had made of their visit to west London, and there could be little arguing that Fulham probably deserved to have given Alvaro Arbeloa his first Premier League win. Nevertheless, it meant more dropped points for United after last weekend’s controversial derby defeat to Manchester City, as well as the draw at Everton and the opening-day loss to Hull. "It’s not been ideal," said Carrick, whose side have won just one of their opening five league games. It is also only the second time in Premier League history United have collected as few as five points from their first five matches.
